sections.title: Phthisis Bulbi: Identification & Pathogenesis
sections.content:
Identification: End-stage ocular response to severe eye injury or disease damage; characterized by a shrunk and non-functional eye.

Pathological Changes: Small, soft, and collapsed eye, opaque and thickened cornea, neovascularization of the iris, cataract, cyclitic membrane, ciliochoroidal detachment, and retinal detachment. In late stages: intraocular calcifications (osseus metaplasia: intraocular bone). Occurs due to hypotony, deranged blood–ocular barrier, and release of cytokines and angiogenic factors.

sections.title: Differential Diagnosis: Causes of Phthisis Bulbi

rows: Open/closed injury, chemical or radiation injury
ROP, OIS, Coat’s, PDR, retinal capillary hemangioma, Sickle cell disease
PHPV, Peters’ anomaly type 2, Norrie disease, FEVR, Incontinentia pigmenti
Retinoblastoma, choroidal melanoma, medulloepithelioma, pineoblastoma, conjunctival spindle cell carcinoma

sections.title: Enucleation: Indications & Complications
content: Indications: Primary intraocular malignancy (Retinoblastoma, Choroidal Melanoma), Painful Blind eye (advanced glaucoma), Severe ocular trauma (risk of sympathetic ophthalmia), Unsightly blind eye, Blind eye with opaque media where carcinoma can't be excluded, Microphthalmia, Endophthalmitis/Panophthalmitis, Phthisis bulbi.

Post-Enucleation Complications: Post-enucleation socket syndrome (PESS), Orbital implant exposure/extrusion/displacement, Oversized implant, Orbital Hematoma, Conjunctival prolapse, Infection/Pyogenic granuloma, Socket/fornix contracture, Dissemination of intraocular neoplasm, Giant Papillary conjunctivitis.

sections.title: Post-Enucleation Socket Syndrome (PESS)
content: Clinical Signs: Deep upper eyelid sulcus, Ptosis, Enophthalmos, Sagging lower lid, Backward tilting of prosthesis leading to ectropion, Eyelid laxity, Upper palpebral papillary conjunctivitis (due to friction).

Management: 1. Treat infection (antibiotics/irrigation). 2. Treat volume/implant issues (Dermal fat graft/larger implant). 3. Correct conjunctival deficiency (mucosa transplant). 4. Correct lid abnormalities (entropion/ectropion/ptosis). 5. Adjust prosthetic.

rows: Single sphere, no direct muscle attachment. Silicone, acrylic.
Wrapped in donor sclera/fascia/bovine pericardium. Muscles sutured to wrap.
Arruga implant. Muscle attached directly. Abandoned due to infection/extrusion.
Hydroxyapatite, Porous polyethylene (Medpor), Bioceramic, Baseball implant, Simple acrylic/silicone spheres, Universal implant, Dermis fat graft.
Loss of superior AND inferior fornix.
All four fornices + reduced horizontal palpebral fissure length.

sections.title: Scenario 5: Clinical Diagnosis
sections.content: Q1: Diagnosis: Retinoblastoma associated with Neurofibromatosis type 1 (indicated by cafe au lait spots). Q2: Histopathology: Small round blue cell tumor, Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes, Homer-Wright rosettes, extensive areas of necrosis and calcification. Q3: Management: Enucleation of the affected eye, multidisciplinary oncology referral, genetic counseling for NF1, and long-term surveillance for secondary neoplasms.
